sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Whole repository preparation
sections.what: Prepares the repository once: it stops if the overhaul branch exists, optionally saves a backup, removes database files and a personal payment identifier from every commit, force-pushes the rewritten history, applies the saved Phase 0 patches as commits under the owner's name, and creates the overhaul branch. It then writes a summary.
sections.why: The header states the aim: keep sensitive data out of all history and start the overhaul from a clean base. A note in the code says a later session will apply any patch that fails here.
sections.watch_out: The force push replaces history on every branch and tag, so anyone with an older copy must re-clone, and no backup is made unless the backup options are set.

summary: A one-time setup script that removes stored database files and a personal payment identifier from the whole repository history, then starts the overhaul branch with the first patches applied.
purpose: Puts the repository into a clean state before the overhaul work begins, and avoids repeating the work once the overhaul branch exists.
why: The header states the goals: keep a private backup, purge sensitive data from all history, commit the owner's Phase 0 patches and create the overhaul branch. The reason for force-pushing is implied, since rewritten history must replace the remote history.
how: Stops if the overhaul branch already exists. Makes a full mirror copy of the repository. Optionally writes a backup bundle. Installs git-filter-repo. Rewrites all history to remove the database files and replace the payment identifier. Searches the rewritten history and file list to confirm both are gone. Force-pushes all branches and tags. Clones the repository fresh, applies each patch from the manifest in order, and commits each one. Removes the patch folder if every patch applied, otherwise keeps the failed ones. Pushes the default branch and creates the overhaul branch. Writes a summary.
inputs: Required environment values: a token, the repository name, the owner's name and the owner id. Optional values: default branch name, a remote address, a private flag, a backup folder and a patch folder. The patch folder holds a manifest file listing each patch and its commit message.
outputs: A rewritten remote history, one commit per applied patch on the default branch, a new overhaul branch, an optional backup bundle, and a summary appended to the step summary file.
risks: Force-pushing replaces the history of every branch and tag, and collaborators must re-clone. A backup is only created if the private flag or backup folder is set. The token is part of the remote address, so it must never be printed.
debug: If it exits saying the overhaul branch exists, nothing was done. If it reports a missing variable, set that value. If the check says the payment identifier or database file is still present, the rewrite missed it; the temporary working folder is not printed, so add a line that prints it before debugging. Failed patches are renamed with FAILED in their file name.
